reflections.body: Bed 4 tonight, 78 years old, sepsis. His wife held his hand the whole shift and kept saying his name like it was a prayer. I titrated his pressors and adjusted his sedation and I was so good at it. That's the thing I can do. I get home at 8am and the apartment is so quiet it hums. I don't know what to write about myself so I write about him.

The intake asked what I want. I said I want to stop feeling like too much for everyone. I hold twelve people's worst days on my chest and I'm calm, I'm the calm one, and then I drive home with the windows down and I can breathe. That drive is the only place I'm honest. Then I close the door and turn everything off.

My sister called. She thinks I'm the strongest person alive. I let her think it. If she saw the rest she'd worry and then I'd have to hold her too, so I keep it light. Todo bien, hermanita. Everything's fine.

Slept four hours. Someone new orient today, I taught her the vent alarms and she said I'm so patient. I am patient with everyone but myself. Noticing that I only exist to other people when I'm useful.
The course talks about the nervous system like weather. Mine has two settings — storm at work, dead calm at home. There's no middle. I don't remember there ever being a middle.

Growing up you learned fast when Mamá's voice went thin. You read the room before you read anything else. I still walk into every space counting the exits and the faces. It's exhausting and it's the only way I know how to be safe.

Good shift. Extubated a young guy, he cried when he could talk again and I cried a little in the med room after and then apologized to no one for it. Why do I apologize for crying when nobody's even there.

I figured out what the calm actually is. It's not calm. I don't go calm — I go gone. When it gets to be too much I just leave my own body standing there and it keeps working, keeps hanging fluids, keeps talking to families, and I'm somewhere behind my own eyes watching. That's not peace. That's the off switch.

Did the worksheet on protections. It asked what the shutdown protects me from. First I wrote 'burnout.' Then I sat with it longer and wrote: from them seeing how much is in there. If they saw the whole ocean they'd back away. So I keep the door shut. Even here I almost didn't write this line.

My sister asked if I was okay in a way that meant she saw something. I changed the subject so fast. Later I realized I do that with everyone. The second someone gets close to my weather I become a weather reporter for someone else.

Windows down on the drive home, 6am, the highway empty, that pink light over the palms. For seven minutes I felt like a person and not a function. Then the garage, then the door, then off. I want more of the seven minutes.

Someone told me I'm 'so composed.' It landed like an accusation. Composed is what I do so no one has to deal with what I actually am. I don't think I've let a single person at work see me rattled in three years.

Trying the orienting exercise from the course. Feet on the floor, name five things. I can do it for a patient's family, coach them through a panic breath. Doing it for myself feels like wearing someone else's coat. Awkward. But I did it. Once.

There was a code today. Young mom. We worked her for forty minutes and I ran it clean, my hands didn't shake, my voice didn't shake. And she didn't make it. I told her husband in the hallway and I held it together and I drove home and I sat in the garage and I could not turn the key off and I could not go inside. I just sat there. I felt everything all at once, todo de golpe, and it was so much I thought it would break something. I'm not overreacting. It was that much. I've spent my whole life being told my too-much is dangerous but tonight the too-much was just grief and it was correct. She was thirty-one. Está bien sentirlo. I'm going to try to believe that.

Couldn't sleep after. Didn't turn off, for once. Just lay there and let it be loud. It didn't kill me. Nobody left because I felt it — but nobody was here to leave, either. I don't know what that proves yet.
Told my sister a real thing. That work was hard this week. Small. But I didn't turn into her weather reporter. She just said 'ay, Sofi' and stayed on the line quiet with me. Nobody backed away.
Off week. Tired in my bones. The apartment hums.
I keep opening this app and closing it. Nothing to say. Fine.

I disappeared. Three weeks, maybe more. Didn't write, didn't answer the check-in, went gone from here too. And I'm looking at it now and — that's the pattern, isn't it. The exact one. Get close to something real, then vanish. I did to this what I do to everyone. I don't even decide it. The door just closes.

Valentina didn't scold me for going quiet. She said the disappearing is information, not failure. I've been chewing on that. If the vanishing is the wound talking then it's not proof I'm broken, it's a place to look. Weird to feel almost tender toward the part of me that runs.

Noticed it live today. Charge nurse asked how I was doing after a rough admit and I felt the door start to swing shut — chin up, deflect, ask about her instead. And I caught the handle. I said 'honestly, that one got to me.' She said 'yeah, me too.' We just stood there being two tired people. It didn't cost me anything. It didn't cost me anything.

The seven minutes on the drive is getting longer. Some days it stretches all the way to the front door and I bring a little of it inside with me. I don't turn off the second I'm home now. Sometimes I make tea and let myself just be a person who had a day.

My sister's visiting next month and I told her I've been 'working on some things.' She didn't make it a big deal. She said she'd always known there was a whole ocean in me and she never thought it was too much, she thought it was why I'm good at what I do. Lloré un poco. In a good way. Maybe the too-much and the good-at-it are the same water.

The world still isn't always safe — I'm a nurse, I know exactly how unsafe. But 'the world isn't safe' isn't the same as 'I have to disappear to survive it.' I can stay in the room now. Some rooms. For a while. That's not nothing. Está bien ser mucho. I'm learning to stay for myself the way I've always stayed for everyone else.

messages.body: hi — signed up. i mostly write at night after shift. i'll probably talk about my patients more than myself, fair warning.
Welcome, Sofía. Writing about your patients is welcome too — sometimes we say the true thing sideways first. I'll be here whenever you're ready to turn the lens around.
figured something out this week. i don't go calm when it's too much. i go gone. wrote it in a reflection if you want to look.
I read it. 'I go gone' is one of the most precise things anyone's said to me about shutdown. That precision is going to serve you. Notice you named it without flinching.
hard shift. wrote about it. it was a lot. sorry if it's too much to read.
It was not too much. It was exactly the right amount for what happened. You stayed in your body and felt it — that's new, and it matters. Be gentle with yourself this week. Estoy aquí.
gracias. i didn't turn off after. first time in a long time.
Checking in — quiet stretch on your end, which is completely okay. No pressure to write. Just wanted you to know the door's still open whenever you want it.
Still here, Sofía. If it's a gone stretch, that's information, not a problem. Come back whenever — nothing's expired.
i'm back. sorry. i disappeared for a few weeks, didn't mean to. saw your messages just now.
No apology needed. You came back — that's the part I'd underline. The disappearing is worth being curious about, not ashamed of. Want to look at it together, gently?
yeah. i think it's the pattern. get close, vanish. i did it to you too. that's kind of a lot to see.
It is a lot to see — and seeing it is exactly how it loosens. You didn't vanish forever this time. You noticed, and you turned around. That's the whole shift, right there.
told a coworker one honest sentence today and the world didn't end. wanted to tell someone.
I'm so glad you told me. 'It didn't cost me anything' — hold onto that data. Your system predicted disaster and got connection instead. Keep collecting those.
my sister said the ocean in me is why i'm good at this, not why i'm too much. i've been carrying that around all week. thought you'd like it.

notes.body: First sessions: presents extraordinarily articulate and warm, then flattens the instant the material turns toward her own interior. Deflects onto patients — a beautiful, functional dodge. Self-named hypervigilance and 'too much'; hasn't yet clocked the caretaking-to-stay-unseen mechanism or how much 'being needed' is doing for her. ICU nurse, over-functions superbly. Origin: translated adult panic as a child. Big feeling = danger arriving. Go slow; she reads rooms faster than I do.

'I don't go calm, I go gone.' Her language for dissociative shutdown is cleaner than most clinicians'. She's ready to name protections; the caretaking piece is starting to surface at the edges. Watch for the crash-after-competence cycle — she over-functions then vanishes alone.

The code (pediatric-adjacent, young mother) cracked something open. Sat in the garage unable to shut off — and crucially, DIDN'T. Stayed in the affect, named it as proportionate rather than pathological ('I'm not overreacting'). This is the most integrated entry to date. Flag: post-breakthrough vulnerability. Her pattern is to disappear right after intimacy with her own feeling. I'd predict a dormant stretch. Will hold the door without chasing.

Three-week silence, as anticipated — the disappearance IS the wound enacting itself. Sent two low-pressure re-engagement notes, no alarm framing. She's returned and, remarkably, metabolized the silence herself: 'that's the pattern, isn't it.' Reframed the vanishing as information rather than failure and it landed. This is the turn. She's beginning to extend to herself the staying-power she's only ever spent on others.

Stage 2 consolidating well. Live catch at work (stayed instead of deflecting; 'it didn't cost me anything' — repeated it, which tells me the old prediction is being overwritten). Sister reframed the 'too much' as source of her competence, and Sofía accepted it in Spanish — she reaches for ES for tenderness, and this time the tenderness was aimed inward. 'The world isn't safe' is loosening into 'I don't have to disappear to survive it.' The drive-home window is lengthening past the front door. Sustain, don't accelerate.
